history.author: Chris Lewis
history.subject: Clean up __osPackRamWriteData
history.message:
Clean up __osPackRamWriteData

Replace the cast-based PIF RAM zeroing loop
(((u32 *)&__osPfsPifRam)[i] = 0) with proper struct member access
(__osPfsPifRam.words[i] = 0) in __osPackRamWriteData, and the identical
pattern in its sibling __osPackRamReadData.

To enable this without an out-of-bounds ramarray[15] access (the loop must
zero all 16 words including pifstatus to match), OSPifRam becomes a union
of its existing {ramarray[15]; pifstatus;} struct and a words[16] view.
The anonymous struct arm preserves all existing .ramarray/.pifstatus
accesses at identical offsets, so every other OSPifRam user is unaffected.

The union arm shares offset 0 with ramarray, so .words[i] compiles to the
same sll/addu/sw sequence as the cast. ROM checksum still matches.

history.author: Claude
history.subject: Fix alSynAllocFX return type in libaudio.h
history.message:
Fix alSynAllocFX return type in libaudio.h

The prototype declared `ALFxRef *alSynAllocFX(...)` (i.e. void **), but the
SGI libaudio API and the function's own return value are `ALFxRef` (void *) —
it returns &s->auxBus[bus].fx[0], a single ALFx pointer. This matches the
adjacent alSynGetFXRef declaration.

Build-safe: alSynAllocFX is still GLOBAL_ASM, and its only caller
(alAudioFrame in synthesizer.c) ignores the return value, so no compiled
code changes.

history.author: Chris Lewis
history.subject: Document measured cause of decompressHuffmanAssetPayload residual
history.message:
Document measured cause of decompressHuffmanAssetPayload residual

decompressHuffmanAssetPayload stays at 99.695% (14 words). Instruction count,
every positional opcode and the frame already match, so the residual is purely
uopt register coloring, and this records what it actually is rather than
another guess.

Measured with an instrumented uopt (ido-static-recomp's uopt.instrumented in a
copy of tools/ido-recomp/linux), gated by checking it reproduces the stock
object byte-identically with its trace variables unset. The copy loop's two
pointer webs tie at save=155 with identical interference neighbour sets, so the
tie breaks on web number and destination colors first; both are blocked from v1
by the copiedByte web, which emits no instruction (ugen coalesces it onto the
temp carrying the loaded byte) yet still reserves v1. The target needs the
copiedByte web colored after the pointers AND the source web colored before the
destination web. The second is free (swapping the two pre-loop initializations);
the first only comes from deleting the copiedByte temp, which changes the loop's
instruction shape. Forcing confirms the limit: forcing either pointer web onto
its target color is force_declined against an interfering holder.

Also capture the generalizable IDO 5.3 -O2 -mips1 findings: t0-t5 are uopt
colors at this level (so a t-register is not evidence of a ugen temp, and the
pool-versus-temp lane labels can mislead); coloring is by descending save with
ties on construction order; save = totalsave/nocs with nocs = ((n-2)>>2)+2,
making it a coarse non-monotone dial; a coalesced-away local still reserves a
register; cfe canonicalizes redundant pointer decoration so there is no pointer
analogue of the redundant-mask lever; declaration order of register-allocated
locals is inert (112 builds, one object); and force_declined against an
interfering holder is a dead end rather than a hint.

Finally, record that this project's decomp-permuter compile.sh mis-scores: it
skips asm-processor and never strips .mdebug, and it reported an apparent 43%
improvement on a candidate whose .text was instruction-words-identical to the
base. Permuter winners must be rebuilt through the project pipeline.

history.author: Chris Lewis
history.subject: Clean up drawCourseDetailsMenu
history.message:
Clean up drawCourseDetailsMenu

Split the collapsed one-liner loop body into readable multi-line
statements and reformat the if/else and second loop body. The
prologue-driving assignments (tiles/yOffset/cursor) plus the for-init
must stay co-located on one line: IDO's ucode scheduler uses source line
numbers as a tie-breaker, so splitting them reorders the prologue.

The remaining decompiler artifacts are load-bearing and now documented:
- volatile unused pins the script[] array at sp+0x70
- cursor[12] with cursor=(s16*)arg0 reproduces the exact address math
- the empty if(arg0 && arg0){} block preserves register allocation

ROM still matches.

history.author: Chris Lewis
history.subject: Improve drawCourseSelectCourseDescription toward the target object
history.message:
Improve drawCourseSelectCourseDescription toward the target object

Object-level comparison against the extracted target (352 instructions)
drops from 316 to 134 differing words and 268 to 50 differing opcodes.

Three measured causes, each read off the target's own encoding:

- The target materialises &gCourseSelectStatus once and reads 0x2c/0x2e
  off it (lhu/lbu), rather than referencing gCourseSelectPurchaseMessageState
  and gCourseSelectExtraCourseColumnState as separate symbols. Using
  COURSE_SELECT_STATUS_LAYOUT reproduces those relocations. The 0x2c read is
  unsigned, but course_select_shop_ui.c needs the signed view of the same
  field, so the layout struct now carries both through a union; existing
  codegen is unchanged and the ROM still matches.

- The extra-course id load relocates against gCourseSelectCourseIds with
  addend 0xf (lbu ...,15(reg)), not against gCourseSelectExtraCourseIds with
  a separate addiu -1. Indexing gCourseSelectCourseIds[4][i - 1] folds the
  offset into the relocation exactly as the target does, removing all six
  relocation mismatches and one instruction.

- The "+++++" branch indexes script[] by the digitCount variable
  (li 3; sll; addu) instead of through a pointer, which IDO otherwise
  constant-folds to &script[3] and hoists. Explicit indices restore the
  three instructions, taking the count from 348 to 351 of 352.

The residual is now a single unresolved uopt allocation decision: the target
colours the CSE'd constant 3 into v1 while we leave it as a ugen temp (t0),
and webs w1-w4 cascade from it. Note the project scorer rates this variant
below the previous attempt because its alignment rewards the old shape; the
relocation table is ground truth, so the score comment records both.

history.author: Chris Lewis
history.subject: Improve drawCourseSelectCourseDescription with a gCourseUnlockPrices live-range fake
history.message:
Improve drawCourseSelectCourseDescription with a gCourseUnlockPrices live-range fake

Object-level residual against the extracted target drops from 134 to 124
differing words and 50 to 28 differing opcodes; structural differences fall
from 13 to 7. The project scorer also improves, 93.202% -> 95.430%.

A code-free double read of gCourseUnlockPrices in the "+++++" branch keeps
the %hi(gCourseUnlockPrices) web live across that branch, which is what makes
IDO hoist the lui the way the target does. Without it we hoist `li 10` and
`li 16` into those two slots instead and materialise the %hi late.

The read count is the dial the field guide describes: one read is inert, two
and three produce the same object, four or more regress. The site is specific
too - the same construct at nine other statement boundaries only regresses.
Found by decomp-permuter, then swept by hand and kept on object evidence
rather than on the permuter's own score.

Remaining residual is still the single uopt colouring decision at the first
divergent row: the target colours the CSE'd constant 3 into v1 where we leave
it in t0.

history.author: Chris Lewis
history.subject: Move the constant 9 into a0 in drawCourseSelectCourseDescription
history.message:
Move the constant 9 into a0 in drawCourseSelectCourseDescription

Object residual drops from 124 to 121 differing words, and the last differing
immediate disappears (constant=0): "li a0,9 / bne a0,v0" now matches the target
register for register.

Two discarded references to the literal 9, placed in the cold purchase-message
block ahead of the load, demote the CSE web for that constant. Per the measured
uopt notes in DECOMPILATION_LEARNINGS.md a discarded read adds occurrences
without adding to totalsave, so it can only lower a web priority - which is
exactly the lever needed here, since our build was colouring the 9 into v1
while the target colours it a0.

Swept as a dial and as a placement: one read is inert, two and three give the
same object, four regress, and the same construct at eight other statement
boundaries only regresses. A 3x3 grid against the gCourseUnlockPrices dial
confirms 121 is the plateau and this is its minimal spelling.

Costs one row: purchaseMessageState moves v0 to v1 at the entry load. Net is
still a clear gain, and the entry row is the next thing to work.

history.author: Chris Lewis
history.subject: Record IDO 5.3 learnings from the drawCourseSelectCourseDescription campaign
history.message:
Record IDO 5.3 learnings from the drawCourseSelectCourseDescription campaign

Four generic findings, each measured across a swept family rather than a
single build:

- A local initialised to a literal is constant-propagated before webs are
  constructed, so a constant carrier cannot recolour a CSE literal. Confirmed
  across six carrier types, two assignment positions, and a graft onto an
  existing dead local; every variant returned a byte-identical object. This
  closes a whole family of plausible levers.

- Subscripting by a variable blocks the constant-fold-and-hoist that the
  equivalent pointer walk invites, which is how the target keeps an index in a
  register when its value is obviously constant.

- A discarded read extends the live range of the %hi web it names, not only
  that web priority, so it can steer where IDO materialises a lui.

- The relocation table distinguishes source spellings that address the same
  byte through adjacent globals, and picking the wrong one drags in extra
  address arithmetic that reads as a structural residual.

Also strengthens the existing rank-on-object-truth note with the magnitude
seen here: the workspace scorer preferred a candidate with six wrong
relocations and 268 of 348 differing opcodes over one with none and 28.

history.author: Chris Lewis
history.subject: Improve drawMenuSpriteClipped match to 90.704%
history.message:
Improve drawMenuSpriteClipped match to 90.704%

Swap the two gMenuSpriteFlipScales lookups so the T increment is read
before the S increment. This is the only source shape found that beats
the previous partial match, taking dist.py's cost from 4616 to 4611.

The function remains under GLOBAL_ASM; the residual is register
allocation. The target carries texS/texT in a2/a3 (move a2,zero /
move a3,zero, then spilled to 128(sp)/124(sp) at each flip-block exit),
which requires table's parameter home store to land in the delay slot of
the scaleY validation branch so a2 is free. Every candidate keeps table
in a2 instead and writes the texture origins straight to memory, which
is exactly the two-instruction shortfall against the target's 496.

Searched and found inert: all 9504 topological orders of the setup
statements, the texture-origin spelling, all 24 clip-bound
initialisation orders, the palette-base spelling, texture-step operand
order, clamp direction, the volatile qualifier, declaration order,
entry-lookup form, padding locals, dimension types, edge expressions,
and edge carriers - about 60,000 variants. Two decomp-permuter passes
found only variants that capture the bottom edge before the clipping
code clamps it, which changes behaviour, and no valid improvement.

Also record three generic learnings: drive sweeps with the project's own
dist.py rather than a proxy metric, a function's codegen is independent
of the rest of its translation unit, and check permuter winners for
stale captures.

history.author: Chris Lewis
history.subject: Improve drawMenuSpriteClipped decompilation to 98.227%
history.message:
Improve drawMenuSpriteClipped decompilation to 98.227%

Replaces the 90.704% NON_MATCHING body with a semantically correct
candidate found by hand analysis plus a decomp-permuter campaign
(nonmatchings/drawMenuSpriteClipped-17/base_47.c, project-compatible
spelling base_74.c). The key lever is a stack of exactly four redundant
& 0xFFFFu masks plus a (short) cast on the flipped texS initialization,
which phase-shifts IDO's temp FIFO into the target's basin while being
runtime-neutral (gSPTextureRectangle masks s to 16 bits). The remaining
1.8% is a single region where the target keeps texS/texT zero-init in
a2/a3 carrier registers with spills duplicated at both flipT-branch
exits; prior campaigns (-12/-13) and ~100k permuter iterations found no
natural typed source reaching it without breaking the 0xA0 frame.

Also records that the defining TU's true signature (u16 image index,
s16 clip bounds) differs from the shared s32/volatile declaration the
matched callers were compiled against; changing the shared prototype
breaks the ROM checksum, confirming a cross-TU prototype mismatch in
the original game.

history.author: Chris Lewis
history.subject: Record IDO shift-folding and memory-forcing levers from drawMenuSpriteWithAlphaClipped campaign
history.message:
Record IDO shift-folding and memory-forcing levers from drawMenuSpriteWithAlphaClipped campaign

Campaign on drawMenuSpriteWithAlphaClipped did not beat the recorded
92.448%, but it isolated the residual to a single register-allocation
swap and produced two generic IDO learnings:

- IDO does not reliably fold consecutive constant left-shifts:
  (x << 3) << 5 emits two sll, while (x << 1) << 1 collapses to one.
  Read the shift decomposition off the target; it is a structural
  (instruction-count) residual, not an allocation one.
- A one-element array declaration (s32 v[1]) demotes a local to a true
  memory variable, freeing its register for whichever variable lost the
  previous allocation round, at the cost of function-wide uopt
  conservatism (early parameter homing, definition-point spills).

Applying both to this function reaches the target's exact instruction
count (449) with opcodes 366->250 and register diffs 425->378, though
the positional dist.py score is lower than the recorded candidate's.

Also repoint the best-match annotation at a workspace that still exists.

history.author: Chris Lewis
history.subject: Improve drawMenuTilemapSprite match to 96.626%
history.message:
Improve drawMenuTilemapSprite match to 96.626%

Two semantics-preserving source changes in the NON_MATCHING candidate:

- commute the operands of sourceOffsetX = tileMask & sourceX
- assign scaleT before scaleS in the flip-scale pair, which moves scaleS onto
  its target register s7

Shift-tolerant distance improves from 252 to 248 instructions.

The remaining residual is one uopt coloring decision: the target colors the
tile palette index into s6 (pushing scaleS/scaleT to s7/s8 and imageIndex out
of the callee-saved band), while every candidate found colors it into t5. That
single difference rotates t6/t7/t8/t9 across roughly 200 instructions of the
GBI macro region.

Also record the macro-mask CSE signedness rule in DECOMPILATION_LEARNINGS.md:
_SHIFTL masks through an unsigned cast, so uopt only CSEs it against a
hand-written (v & mask) when the carrier's own type is unsigned.

history.author: Chris Lewis
history.subject: Record measured cause of drawScaledAssetTableSprite residual
history.message:
Record measured cause of drawScaledAssetTableSprite residual

Score is unchanged at 97.235% (893 differences, object sha1 a5b43f2878af);
this commit removes fake scaffolding that measurement proved inert and
records the mechanism behind the remaining residual.

Reading IDO's pre-as1 output (cc -S) localises the whole residual to two
register decisions. The target colors the scale as $9 and the right bound as
$10, and pairs the sprite geometry per axis (v0=width, v1=scaled width,
a0=height, a1=scaled height). The recorded candidate reverses the first pair;
the "if (scale && scale) {}" artifact buys the target's early scale spill and
its $2/$3 height/maxY pool pair but forces that reversal, and removing the
artifact flips both lanes together. Roughly 4000 artifact variants never
produced scale in $9 together with the early spill. The per-axis v0/v1/a0/a1
pairing is a separate wall: across 300 randomised source shapes the two field
loads always take the low register pair and the two shift results the high
pair, independent of statement order, declaration order, scoping, expression
grouping, and source line layout.

Proven inert and therefore dropped from the NON_MATCHING body, each verified
byte-identical: the "if (1) {}" block, the "spriteWidth = 1 << (scale + 10),
spriteWidth" dead-variable reuse, and "sprite[1].field" plus a later
"sprite++" (now &asset->entries[i] and sprite->field). The volatile on
entryIndex and the & 0xFFFFu mask are load-bearing and stay.

Also cleared as causes: the workspace flag gap against the project preset,
compiling in the real translation unit, K&R definition form, the matched
sibling's named-bound-locals idiom, early-return control flow, separate
shift/scaled-size carriers, CSE'd inline field reads, and 240 local
declaration permutations.

history.author: Chris Lewis
history.subject: Record measured cause of drawScaledAssetTableSpriteWithExplicitPalette residual
history.message:
Record measured cause of drawScaledAssetTableSpriteWithExplicitPalette residual

The t1/t2 inversion that has held this function (and its sibling
drawScaledAssetTableSprite) at a 33-word residual is one quotient crossing
1.0 in uopt's colouring priority, confirmed with the instrumented IDO 5.3
uopt gated against the stock object:

  with the `if (scale && scale) {}` filler:  save = 5.0/6 = 0.833 -> the
      right-clip-bound web is decided first and takes t1; the scale web
      splits and its piece takes t2.
  without it:                               save = 5.0/5 = 1.000 -> ties
      the bound web, wins the tie on ascending web number, takes t1.
      Both registers then match the target.

totalsave is 5.0 either way: the filler's reads are discarded, so they add
occurrences (crossing the nocs 5->6 step) without adding any saving. The
filler is load bearing for the instruction count, though - removing it also
drops three schedule artifacts the target has (two unfilled delay slots and
one recomputed compare), so the two halves cannot yet be had together.

Adds the generic corollary to DECOMPILATION_LEARNINGS.md: a discarded read
is a pure priority penalty on the web it reads, so a dead-conditional filler
is not allocation-neutral for the variable it names.

Also corrects the earlier "pool-versus-temp class crossing" reading of the
table-base register: t0-t5 are uopt-colored at -O2, so that difference is
web ordering, not web formation.

Campaign: 2008 gated builds over eleven source families (statement order,
shift carrier, pointer/palette spelling, declaration topology, homolog clip
idiom, frame-neutral named bounds, filler expression x position, setup
interleaving, physical line grouping, K&R parameters, F3DEX-preserving
permuter). All floor at 33 words; no candidate reproduces the target's
`move t4,a2`. probe-lines reports LINE-SENSITIVE with a clean control, but
every line grouping is inert. No improvement on the project's scorer, so the
recorded best match is left unchanged.

history.author: Chris Lewis
history.subject: Match func_80001584 (controller-pak init & repair-id retry count)
history.message:
Match func_80001584 (controller-pak init & repair-id retry count)

func_80001584 initializes the controller pak for a given channel via
osPfsInitPak, then calls osPfsRepairId; if the result is PFS_ERR_ID_BROKEN
(4) or PFS_ERR_ID_FATAL (0xA) it bumps a per-channel retry counter at
D_800EC9D8[channel]. D_800E4C40 is an OSPfs array (one per channel, 104
bytes each), so it is now declared as an array and indexed by channel.

To match IDO 5.3's 0x20-byte stack frame exactly, the pfs local's address
is taken (OSPfs **sp18 = &pfs) so IDO allocates it in the addressed-locals
region; this is an IDO frame-layout quirk in the same spirit as
func_800340D8's struct-locals padding.

history.author: Chris Lewis
history.subject: Match func_8000BEC0 (course select menu transition start)
history.message:
Match func_8000BEC0 (course select menu transition start)

Decompiled the course-select transition-start routine that initializes the
menu fade timer, kicks off the background/course preview update callback,
seeds the chosen-course lookup table value, and runs the per-object update
loop before queuing the next transition handler.

Notable: D_8010AF72/D_8010AF73 are read unsigned (lbu via u8 cast), and
D_800B34E0 is indexed as a u16[][7] table by (u8)D_8010AF73*7 + D_8010AF72.
IDO's scheduler was picky about line grouping of the loop preamble, so the
call/assignment/do-header share one line.

history.author: Chris Lewis
history.subject: Match func_8000C114 (course select menu transition)
history.message:
Match func_8000C114 (course select menu transition)

Course-select analog of func_80005468: fades the menu out and, once the
exit mode is set, tears down the scene and counts unfilled selection
slots, setting a flag when all slots are decided.

The slot-counting loop walks adjacent BSS symbol labels (&D_800EC9F1 ..
&D_800EC9F9) with a stride-4 byte pointer. IDO aggressively unrolls
structured counted loops over runtime-computed address ranges (subu +
andi remainder idiom), so the loop is written as an unstructured goto
loop collapsed inside a do { ... } while (0) to emit the plain do-while
the original shipped.

history.author: Chris Lewis
history.subject: Match func_800152D0 (title menu list-item scroll-out state machine)
history.message:
Match func_800152D0 (title menu list-item scroll-out state machine)

func_800152D0 is the update callback for the menu list item created by
func_80015404. It scrolls the item in (state 0), spawning the next item
(func_800157B4) when x reaches 0x70 and transitioning to a wait state at
x == -0x50; waits (state 1); then scrolls out (state 2), signalling the
spawned child to advance when x reaches -0x70.

Key matching details:
- Extended MenuItemActor with a self-referential child pointer at 0x20,
  shared by func_80015404 (constructor) and func_800152D0 (updater).
- switch (arg0->state) with the literal 1 stored to D_801235B4 lets IDO
  keep v1=1 live from the dispatch delay slot and reuse it for the store.
- Declared func_80072138 with its real s32 return (it returns 0) in this
  TU; the discarded return still steers x into v1 to match the target.
- Named local for arg0->child to land the child pointer in v0.

history.subject: Match func_80022198 (character select text draw)
history.message:
Match func_80022198 (character select text draw)

Draw the character-select widget's text via func_80013154. The text buffer
is selected by a mode global (D_80121B5E): three fixed-stride text tables
(D_800B67D8/0x74, D_800B6934/0x60, D_800B6A54/0x70) indexed by
(u16)D_80121B50, or a default buffer (D_800B6B34) when out of range.

Key match detail: referencing D_80121B5E directly in each condition (rather
than caching in a local) makes IDO 5.3 emit 'lui a1; lbu a1(a1)' with the
destination register doubling as the lui base, instead of a separate v0
scratch.

history.message:
Match func_80022274 (character select widget update state machine)

Decompiled the character select widget update callback. It is an 8-state
transition state machine (timer wait, sprite scale-in, x-position slide
in/out driven by the D_80121D88 menu-flow variable) that delegates to the
func_80022198 draw callback via func_800483FC, or destroys the actor via
func_800716E4 once it reaches the terminal state.

Pattern follows the already-matched sibling func_80021C98 / func_80020DEC.
The per-state codegen required the timer increment to be written as a
compound-expression condition (++timer == 2) so IDO reuses the incremented
register instead of reloading it.

history.subject: Match func_80023198 (character select widget scroll-in state machine)
history.message:
Match func_80023198 (character select widget scroll-in state machine)

A sibling of func_800219E4. Slides the widget in to a mode-dependent x
threshold (-0x88 normally, -0x8A when D_800EC9C2 indicates certain game
modes / D_80121B5E == 0), waits for a transition signal (D_80121D88 ==
3 or 7), then scrolls it back off-screen and destroys the actor.

The threshold check reads two globals; the target loads D_800EC9C2 into
v0 inline and D_80121B5E into v1. Hoisting only the second global into a
local () while referencing the first inline reproduces
IDO's exact register choice and the unreachable dead `li v0,-0x88` after
the true-branch store.

history.author: Chris Lewis
history.subject: Match func_80027498 (course select widget scroll-out state machine)
history.message:
Match func_80027498 (course select widget scroll-out state machine)

func_80027498 is the CourseSelectWidgetActor member of the scroll-out
state-machine family (twin of func_8002C390): case 0 fades the sprite in
(spriteIndex += 0x26 up to 0x100), case 1 waits for the transition trigger
(D_80121D88 == 3 || D_801235B8->screenState == 9), case 2 slides out
(x += 0x20) terminating with func_800716E4/func_800291F0(7).

The structurally-correct body matched 96.6% with only register-allocation
differences. The permuter found the 100% fix: reload state = arg0->state once
*after* the switch rather than per-case, which lets IDO keep the live state in
v1 and emit a memory reload on the case-2 path.

history.subject: Match func_8002A27C
history.message:
Match func_8002A27C

Widget state machine in player_count_select_ui. The top-level logic is an
if/else-if/else chain with short-circuit && over (D_80121B5E vs spriteIndex)
and a y-position check, followed by a 6-entry switch jump table (cases 0-5).

Key details for the match:
- (u16) cast on the s16 spriteIndex field so IDO loads it via lhu, not lh
- inline the field access so D_80121B5E is loaded into v0 first
- int state (not u8) for the switch scratch to match register allocation
- explicit empty case 0 / case 5 to force the jump table

Match func_8002C800

func_8002C800 initializes a shop-menu row actor (s16[5] icon positions at
0x18, iconY at 0x22, state bytes at 0x24/0x25/0x26) and registers
func_8002C624 as its callback via func_80071824. It is the shop-menu twin

0x3E000, unk18 += 0xFFF60000) using var_v0 = (unk2A < 5) ? 1 : -1, else it

history.author: Chris Lewis
history.subject: Decompile func_8003969C
history.message:
Decompile func_8003969C

State-machine sibling of func_80039610 in src/3A0E0.c. Reads a u16 counter at
arg0+0x2A; on func_80041FB4(3)==1 it increments and, when it hits 0x14, resets
to 0 and reschedules func_80039610 (state 0x58). Otherwise bumps arg0->unk20
by 0x80000. Always republishes position via func_8004209C and func_800428C8.

Matched 100% via permuter after a 98.6% hand attempt — the residual diffs were
pure register allocation in the counter block. Masking the u16 load explicitly
(& 0xFFFF) and storing through a pointer variable / mask variable reproduces
IDO's exact t6/t7/t8 register sequence, mirroring the already-matched
func_80039610 source form.

Matching relied on declaring the counter as s32 and using a compound
assignment (temp = (arg0->unk2A += 1)) so IDO keeps the unmasked sum for
the store and the masked sum for both divisions, avoiding spurious moves.

State-machine sibling of func_80039E5C in src/3A0E0.c. Decompile the

$t7 for the counter load, IDO reused $v0).

- a semantically-noop mask that pushes IDO off the $v0 reuse onto the
sequential $t6/$t7/... allocation. Split Struct3A0E0's pad24 to expose the
unk2A/unk2C fields at the correct offsets.

Match func_8003DBE8

Decompiled main_menu_effects.c:func_8003DBE8 to 100%.

The function increments animFrame, masks it to a 1-bit toggle, and
decrements angleVelocity (via a hoisted base pointer into the
MainMenuEffectActor.angle sub-struct) when the toggle hits zero,
switching to the func_8003DBB8 callback once angleVelocity reaches 0x10.

materialises as addiu v0,a0,0x20 / lh 2(v0) when the pointer assignment
is hoisted out of the conditional into the unconditional function body;
placing it inside the if lets IDO fold it to direct 0x22(a0) addressing.
Same pattern as the sibling func_8003DCCC.

history.author: Chris Lewis
history.subject: Match func_80045990
history.message:
Match func_80045990

Sibling of the already-matched func_800459D4: indexes an 8-byte-element
table, computing temp_v0 = arg0 + *(s32*)(arg0+4)*8 (then +=8), but reads
its shift amount from the table (lhu 0xC(temp_v1) << 5) rather than taking
it as an argument, so it has one fewer parameter.

Key codegen facts:
- The u16 index parameter produces the dummy 'sw a1, 4(sp)' (s32 + explicit
  & 0xFFFF does not).
- A short-typed array index (idx = 1) is what triggers the trailing dead
  'addiu v1, v1, 8'; temp_v1[1].field folds the +8 into the displacement
  and omits it. Found via decomp-permuter.

history.author: Chris Lewis
history.subject: Merge func_80048E60 and func_80048E80 into one function
history.message:
Merge func_80048E60 and func_80048E80 into one function

func_80048E60 falls through (no jr $ra) into func_80048E80, which reuses
the $t7 register loaded at the end of func_80048E60 and is never called
via jal. They are a single function that splat split at the 464E0/49A80
subsegment boundary.

Move the boundary from 0x49A80 to 0x49C00 (func_80049000) so the whole
function lives in one segment, give func_80048E60 an explicit size:0x1A0
so splat extracts it as one 0x80048E60-0x80049000 function, rename the
shifted segment 49A80.c -> 49C00.c, and remove the obsolete
func_80048E80 stub. ROM checksum still matches.

history.author: Chris Lewis
history.subject: Match func_8004FA44
history.message:
Match func_8004FA44

Decompiled func_8004FA44, which initializes an object's three position
fields (0x18/0x1C/0x20) as a base array value plus a randomized offset
from func_800430D0(), then registers func_8004F9CC as its update callback.

Reached a 100% match. The only non-trivial detail was operand order in
the final add: writing (array_value + shift) rather than (shift +
array_value) flips IDO's register allocation to match the target across
all three blocks. Control flow, instruction selection, and the per-call
reload of the 0x10 index were all straightforward.

history.author: Chris Lewis
history.subject: Match func_80054AC0
history.message:
Match func_80054AC0

The decrementing counterpart to func_80054A04: each tick adds field 0x24
into 0x18 and decrements 0x24 by 4. When 0x24 reaches zero it sets the
0x28 counter to 0x1E and reassigns the callback to func_80054A64.
Written in the field-mutation style of func_80057B60 so IDO keeps the
subtracted value in a register (bnez) instead of folding (temp - 4) == 0
into temp == 4. 100% assembly match.

history.author: Chris Lewis
history.subject: Decompile func_8005638C
history.message:
Decompile func_8005638C

func_8005638C clamps the delta (arg1 - arg0->unk24) to [-0x2000, 0x2000]
and adds it to arg0->unk24. Reading the struct field inline in the
subtraction (instead of hoisting it into a named temp) makes IDO place
the load in $v1 and the diff in $v0, matching the target. The compound
assignment schedules the addu into the branch delay slot and produces
the li+addu clamped path.

history.author: Chris Lewis
history.subject: Match func_800601F8 (race UI bounce/scroll update)
history.message:
Match func_800601F8 (race UI bounce/scroll update)

Decompiled func_800601F8, a race-UI effect update callback. When
D_80121B56 is 0 it advances the actor's position fields (0x18/0x1C/0x20)
by velocity fields (0x48/0x4C/0x50), decrements the 0x4C velocity by
0x8000, and increments the 0x54 counter; at >=0x10 it calls func_800716E4,
otherwise it re-schedules via func_800483FC using either the
func_8005FBA8 or func_8005FED0 callback based on the 0x57 flag.

Match uses the raw pointer-arithmetic style of the neighbouring
func_8006069C. The only diff beyond control flow was register allocation;
placing the 0x54 counter increment after the 0x4C decrement (both
independent statements) reproduced the target's scheduling for a 100%
match.

Match func_8006713C

Counts elements in the D_800D91E8[D_80121B50] list (terminated by a -1
sentinel at element offset 0x2), storing the count into arg0->unk1E,
then allocates a texture/display list and sets up a callback. Same shape

counter.

A 100% match required keeping arg0 live in callee-saved s0 across the
trailing jal calls; achieved by introducing a local alias of the
argument (new_var = arg0) at the top of the function.

history.message:
Match func_8006F984 (race camera focus-from-player update)

Race camera update that copies the player's cameraPos into the camera's
focus and then invokes the shared stride-driven update func_8006D8B4.

IDO 5.3 only keeps the 0x60C stride in a single register (a1) when the
playerIndex*stride multiply explicitly references the stride variable.
Plain array indexing (sizeof-derived multiply) makes IDO spill the stride
to a2 for the multiplies and load a1 separately for the call, so the
access is written as stride-based pointer arithmetic, which is the
codebase's natural form (func_8006D8B4 takes the stride as a parameter).

history.author: Chris Lewis
history.subject: Decompile func_8008C704
history.message:
Decompile func_8008C704

Zeroes a per-player field (offset 0x582, stride 0x60C) across the four
player globals, then when D_80121B56 is clear calls func_80084730 on each,
func_8007B250, and iterates func_8008C7D0 over D_80121B54 players.

Matched at 100% by writing the player loop as a strength-reduced indexed
for-loop (base + i * 0x60C) instead of an explicit pointer-bump do/while,
which lets IDO keep the base in $a0 for the top region and reload it fresh
into $s1 at loop entry.

history.author: Chris Lewis
history.subject: Match func_80097AE8
history.message:
Match func_80097AE8

Match the sine-table lookup function in src/98680.c. Two codegen tricks
were needed for IDO -O2 -mips1:
- Reassign the masked angle back to the s16 parameter so the value stays
  in a0's home register (reproducing move/andi/sra a0 plus the dead arg
  homing store).
- Capture the shifted table value in a named local before returning, so
  the >>3 lands in a temp (t2) and only the final s16 narrowing reaches v0.

history.author: Chris Lewis
history.subject: Match func_800994F4
history.message:
Match func_800994F4

Decompiled the task-node setup function in 99980.c. It calls
func_80099384 to allocate a Node99980 and, on success, populates the
node's fields from its arguments (type, callback, priority) and sets a
state field to 2.

Achieved 100% match. The only non-trivial detail was statement order:
writing the constant store (unk16 = 2) after the arg-derived stores
causes IDO to allocate the constant temp last, matching the target's
register choice and delay-slot scheduling.

history.author: Chris Lewis
history.subject: Decompile func_8009CCC0
history.message:
Decompile func_8009CCC0

Variable-length sequence value reader in 9CE70.c. Reads a 1- or 2-byte
value (high bit set => ((b0 & 0x7F) << 8) | b1), stores it as u16 at
arg0 + 0xCC, and returns the advanced read pointer.

100% match. Two harmless register-allocation artifacts were needed:
split the shift as ((v & 0x7F) << 1) << 7, and load the second byte
through a named temp (v |= *(new_var = arg1)).

history.author: Chris Lewis
history.subject: Decompile func_8009D308
history.message:
Decompile func_8009D308

Matches a command-stream callback that reads a byte index from arg1,
looks up an offset in the table at arg0->unk54 + 0x14, and stores the
base+offset pointer into arg0->unk70. The double inline read of
arg0->unk54 is an intentional IDO codegen quirk needed for correct
register allocation (base in $a2).

history.author: Chris Lewis
history.subject: Decompile func_8009D40C
history.message:
Decompile func_8009D40C

Byte-transform-then-add event handler: reads a byte, calls func_8009F4C8,
stores the result at arg0+0xEF, then stores result+next_byte there. Sibling
of func_8009D3BC/func_8009D45C (which target fields 0x118/0xF2).

100% match. A clean two-temp version reached 98.7% but IDO mis-allocated
the result/byte registers; routing the result through the byte temp inline
in the add expression (temp_a0 = temp_v0) reproduces the target's
move/lbu/addu register sequence exactly.

history.author: Chris Lewis
history.subject: Decompile func_8009F748
history.message:
Decompile func_8009F748

memset-like byte fill. Key insight: the 2nd parameter is an
unsigned char, which IDO homes to its stack slot (the dead
sw $a1,4($sp) with no prologue) and masks with andi. The
while(n--) form avoids IDO's -O2 memset unrolling and leaves
the expected dead move shadow of the post-decrement value.

history.author: Chris Lewis
history.subject: Declare main menu public interface in main_menu.h
history.message:
Declare main menu public interface in main_menu.h

Add include/main_menu.h declaring all functions defined in
src/main_menu.c. Include it from main_menu.c and the callers
(game_boot, race_flow, controller_rumble, controller_pak_menu_flow),
removing their now-redundant local externs.

Resolved two caller/callee signature inconsistencies against the
definitions in main_menu.c: func_80000A40 and func_80000C48 take u16
(not s32) in the definition, so the header and all callers now use u16.

Signatures for the GLOBAL_ASM functions without an in-source C body were
derived from their assembly (argument registers and return-value use).

history.author: Chris Lewis
history.subject: Declare main menu debug UI public interface in main_menu_debug_ui.h
history.message:
Declare main menu debug UI public interface in main_menu_debug_ui.h

Add include/main_menu_debug_ui.h with prototypes for the public entry
points defined in src/main_menu_debug_ui.c (func_8003BBBC, func_8003BEB4).
Both are effect-task initializers; their argument types (EndObjTask,
DebugObjectPositionTask) are forward-declared opaquely in the header, with
the full struct definitions remaining private to the .c via tagged structs.

This fixes a caller/callee type inconsistency: race_to_main_menu_transition.c
declared func_8003BBBC as taking no arguments (extern void func_8003BBBC(void))
while the definition takes an EndObjTask*. Replace that local extern with the
header include so callers see the correct signature.

history.author: Chris Lewis
history.subject: Declare main menu effects public interface in main_menu_effects.h
history.message:
Declare main menu effects public interface in main_menu_effects.h

Add include/main_menu_effects.h declaring the 14 functions defined in src/main_menu_effects.c that are referenced from other translation units: six spawn entry points and eight callback initialisers. The actor type is forward-declared as an opaque struct, matching the main_menu_debug_ui.h convention.

Several callers previously declared these functions with widened s32 parameter types that disagreed with the actual s16/u8 definitions in main_menu_effects.c. The shared header now exposes the correct types and the callers local externs are removed in favour of the include. All call sites pass constants, so the ABI-level argument setup is unchanged and the ROM still matches.

history.author: James Lewis
history.subject: Match osSyncPrintf/rmonPrintf at the real address (0x800A3580)
history.message:
Match osSyncPrintf/rmonPrintf at the real address (0x800A3580)

The pre-existing `osSyncPrintf = 0x80048E4C` symbol was mislabeled. ROM
disassembly shows 0x80048E4C is a lone arg-saving stub wedged in game
display-list code (neighbor func_80048E60 references D_800EC9C2), not part of
a matching pair.

The real libultra syncprintf.c lives at 0x800A3580 / 0x800A359C: two
byte-identical empty-varargs stubs inside the libc block, between
ultra/libc/sprintf (0xA4100) and ultra/libc/ll (0xA41C0) -- the textbook
osSyncPrintf + rmonPrintf TU.

Changes:
- Reassign `osSyncPrintf` to 0x800A3580 and add `rmonPrintf` at 0x800A359C in
  symbol_addrs.txt (0x80048E4C reverts to an auto-named game func).
- yaml: 0x49A40 back to plain asm (game code); 0xA4180 becomes
  `c, ultra/libc/syncprintf`.
- Add src/ultra/libc/syncprintf.c (two empty stubs); matches at -O2.
- Document the mislabel pitfall in DECOMPILATION_LEARNINGS.md.

ROM still matches (build-and-verify.sh -> OK).

history.author: Chris Lewis
history.subject: Record IDO 5.3 learnings from the resolveRacePlayerCollisionVolumes campaign
history.message:
Record IDO 5.3 learnings from the resolveRacePlayerCollisionVolumes campaign

Ran a full campaign against the 99.638% residual (128 measured variants plus
a permuter run with a corrected scorer). No variant beat the inherited
candidate, so the assembly include stays; the stale workspace reference in
the source comment is repointed at a workspace that still exists.

The residual is 38 differing instruction words with the instruction count
(1314) and frame size (-736) already exact: four contested registers in each
matrix-axis loop, and one dead `move reg,zero` plus a coalescing copy in the
child-volume loop.

New generic notes:
- naming a strength-reduced array cursor folds the member offset into the
  cursor and changes the address arithmetic, so a large load/store
  displacement is evidence the cursor is IDO's own induction variable;
- substituting the local that carries a loop index has global blast radius,
  shifting register assignment from the first instructions of the function;
- statement line numbers are inert in this project's no-`-g` builds, so the
  line-assignment lever family can be skipped after a blank-line control.

history.author: Chris Lewis
history.subject: Match saveRaceRecordReplayData
history.message:
Match saveRaceRecordReplayData

The residual was a single uopt colouring difference: the hoisted literal 8
took a1 where the target uses a3 (3 instruction words).

An instrumented uopt trace identified the value as a hoisted-literal web whose
split ladder piece is coloured lowest-free-index. The local assigned in the
last accumulation-ladder blocks carries its web forward into the replay copy
phase and so forbids its own colour to that piece. With `count` as the scratch
for every slot, a3 (count's colour) is blocked and the literal falls to a1;
using `writeIndex` - not yet live - for the two extra-course slots blocks a1
instead and frees a3, so 8 takes a3 and 9 takes t0 as in the target.

The function only reaches the 803-instruction basin when
gPackedRaceRecordReplayBuffer is defined in this translation unit rather than
referenced through the header extern, so its bss symbol moves out of
bss_chunk_a_2_ending_credits_flow_tail into a .bss split for this file.

Verified with ./tools/build-and-verify.sh: build/snowboardkids.z64 OK.

history.subject: Improve updateCharacterSelectCourseMenu to a 2-byte partial match
history.message:
Improve updateCharacterSelectCourseMenu to a 2-byte partial match

Give character_select_course_menu.c ownership of its BSS range: define
gCharacterSelectCourseExitOptionIndex and the cursor state union in the
TU, split the .bss segment at 0x8010AE80 in snowboardkids.yaml, and add
an alias linker script for the individual cursor state symbols. With the
union defined in the same translation unit, IDO shares one lui across the
paired cursor state/sprite index stores, matching the target's shared-at
codegen at all three sites.

Also fix the repeat timer overflow path: the modulo needs a signed cast
to reproduce the full signed-division guard, and the timer reset is a
chained assignment through the variable.

The remaining diff is a single register choice (li a1,0xC vs li t5,0xC)
plus its store, so the pragma stays in place with the improved body under
NON_MATCHING.

history.author: Chris Lewis
history.subject: Improve updateCharacterSelectMenu match to 99.919% (frame now exact)
history.message:
Improve updateCharacterSelectMenu match to 99.919% (frame now exact)

The residual was never a register-allocation problem: pool (117/117) and temp
(84/84) lanes, opcodes and instruction count were already identical at the
previous 99.811% best. The whole difference was the stack frame, -144 against
the target's -136.

Calibrated IDO 5.3's frame layout on this function against the compiler's own
-g3 .mdebug symbol table: locals are top-anchored at the frame size and packed
top-down in declaration order, the block's size is set by the deepest local
that actually needs memory, and F = round8(64 + T + L) with T_min = 40 for this
instruction stream. That pins the target's declared-locals block at exactly 32
bytes, so three measured byte-inert simplifications close the frame:

  - delete `unused`, which was never referenced                     -1 byte
  - merge nextRepeatTimer into leftRepeatTimer, whose live ranges
    are disjoint (now repeatTimerScratch)                           -2 bytes
  - inline heldRight as otherPlayerIndex & (STICK_RIGHT | R_JPAD)   -4 bytes

plus dropping the redundant leading `maximumIndex = 5;`. 40 -> 32 bytes of
locals takes the frame from -144 to -136 and the residual from 8 words to 6.

The six remaining words are two stack offsets. Because the block bottom is
0x68, no declared local can live at 0x64, so the original carries the u16
roster bound in a compiler expression temp rather than a named local. Roughly
thirty source families were measured against that and all are refuted -
declaration order and scope, register, s16/s32/u8/array/struct carriers, no-op
and masking wrappers, ternary and dead-read CSE seeding, and a cached-flag
loop-invariant meant to give uopt's LICM something memory-free to hoist (uopt
does not hoist control flow out of a loop). A 2400s decomp-permuter sweep
returned nothing better than the hand candidate.

campaign-findings.md records the frame law, the proof that L must be 32, the
dead-family table, and the one open mechanical question, so this is picked up
from evidence rather than re-searched.

Full ROM build and SHA1 verification pass.

Clean up updateCharacterSelectPlayerStatsPanels

Replace raw byte-pointer magic offsets with proper struct access while

history.author: Chris Lewis
history.subject: Improve updateCourseSelectCourseList match
history.message:
Improve updateCourseSelectCourseList match

The recorded 86.365% figure did not reproduce: it was measured in a
workspace whose target object still used the pre-rename symbol names and
whose candidate carried its own local type definitions. Rebuilt against a
fresh workspace, the in-tree body scored 68.440%. This rebuilds it to
84.857% on that same footing.

The dominant residual was addressing form, not register allocation. The
target emits a fresh `lui $at,%hi(S)` before every `%lo(S+k)` store in the
course-select status reset, which IDO only does when each slot is its own
global; one aggregate makes uopt promote `&S` to a base register and switch
to `off(base)`. Splat labels every address inside a sized symbol as `S+k`,
so the consolidation was invisible in the extracted asm. Split
gCourseSelectStatus back into its 32 per-player scalars and keep the
aggregate spelling for the translation units that index it with a variable
via an overlay macro. The five trailing cursor fields do address off a
materialized base in the target, which is what the CourseSelectStatusLayout
cast produces, so both spellings are reproduced.

Two further addresses needed a second name to stop IDO value-numbering two
reads into one: the selected course id and the highlighted column. Both are
linker-script aliases onto existing storage, so the linked bytes are
unchanged. Also corrected the local enqueueSoundEffect prototype to the
(s16, s16) form the definition in sound_manager.c actually uses, which is
what produces the sll/sra narrowing on the shared literal 1.

The remaining ~15% is IDO declining to cache global loads across blocks
where our build does, concentrated in the up/down column handling.

Verified: ./tools/build-and-verify.sh, ROM SHA1 matches.

history.author: Chris Lewis
history.subject: Improve updateCourseSelectCourseList match to 86.998%
history.message:
Improve updateCourseSelectCourseList match to 86.998%

Continues the addressing-form work: the residual was IDO value-numbering two
reads of one global into a single load where the target reloads. uopt numbers
by object, so two declarations of the same address never merge, and the
original source evidently had two for the highlighted column, the selected
course id, and the held-pad state read by the repeat logic. Added the third
alias (gMenuInputHeld) and placed each alias only at the references the
target actually reloads; aliasing every reference scored worse than aliasing
three of them.

Also switched the unlock-state block to read the selection through
gRacePlayers[playerIndex], which is how the target reaches it: off the base
register the surrounding indexed accesses already materialized, rather than
through a folded %lo.

The candidate now emits 881 of the target 884 instructions with a matching
-0x48 frame; the alignment gap count drops from 238 to 72. What is left is
gMenuInputRepeatTimers being base-promoted in the choice-prompt arm where the
target folds each access. That did not respond to splitting or aliasing the
symbol, which fits promotion being register-availability driven rather than
name driven, so it is downstream pressure from elsewhere in the arm.

history.author: Chris Lewis
history.subject: Improve updateMultiplayerCourseSelectMenu match to 99.210%
history.message:
Improve updateMultiplayerCourseSelectMenu match to 99.210%

Raises the recorded best from 98.696% and, more importantly, changes the
kind of residual: the object comparison against the target is now a pure
allocation-mismatch with 0 opcode mismatches and 0 alignment gaps, at the
exact instruction count (836) and frame size (0xB0). Positional word
mismatches fall 180 -> 94.

Three changes, each measured independently:

- Spell the visible-player loop as an explicit `playerIndex = 0; while
  (...)` instead of a `for`. This removes the rotation in the unrolled
  four-player store block and takes alignment gaps from 8 to 6.

- Add three discarded reads of gPlayerCount at the head of the else
  branch. They emit no instructions but add occurrences to that variable's
  web, which orders it ahead of the &gRacePlayers[gPlayerCount] end
  pointer in IDO's colouring pool; without them the two webs swap a0/a1
  across the whole branch. The dial is inert below three reads and
  identical above three.

- Carry a redundant playerIndex cursor in the final camera loop. Keeping
  that variable live to the end of the function reproduces the target's
  allocation for the entire per-player block and dissolves a
  three-instruction scheduling rotation about 700 instructions upstream.

Ruled out along the way, with evidence: statement line assignment (probe
lines reports the residual unreachable by reflow, and 22 --tie probes move
0 sites toward the target), dropping the visible loop's own init, read
dials on finishedPlayerCount, a named local for the scan end bound, and
five spellings of a carrier for gPlayerInputHeld.

The remaining 94 words are register assignment only: two pairwise pool
swaps and a temp-ring rotation, plus two camera spill-slot constants.

history.subject: Match updateMultiplayerCourseSelectMenu

Match updateMultiplayerCourseSelectMenu

Replace the GLOBAL_ASM include and 99.210% NON_MATCHING draft with a byte-exact C implementation. Starting from a 99.375% decomp.me scratch contributed by inspectredc, complete the match by correcting project symbol names and indices and reproducing the original loop variable liveness.

unattributed_commits.subject: Match 284 functions across 15 files
unattributed_commits.message:
Match 284 functions across 15 files

Decompile 284 #pragma GLOBAL_ASM stubs into byte-exact matching C across
15 src/ files. Matched in parallel across 5 isolated git worktrees, each
verified byte-exact (build.sh/diff.sh) and via full-ROM build-and-verify.

Per file: 57EA0 (78), 8CAB0 (25), 33680 (24), 1C970 (21), 3CAF0 (20),
37FE0 (19), 3A0E0 (18), 54260 (15), 73830 (15), 2D0E0 (13), 9CE70 (12),
6A490 (11), 464E0 (6), 4E760 (4), 24480 (3).

The dominant idiom is a field-setter + state-callback wrapper (write
struct fields, then func_80071824(actor, &next_state)); matching hinges
on store order and field signedness (lhu->u16 vs lh->s16). No shared
include/ edits; all declarations and typedefs are file-local.

unattributed_commits.subject: Improve 4 race_ui_effects.c functions, fix a broken symbol reference
unattributed_commits.message:
Improve 4 race_ui_effects.c functions, fix a broken symbol reference

func_80059A04: 96.586% -> 97.714% (the tracked comment was stale/
unverifiable, referencing a workspace that no longer exists)
func_8005A4BC: 96.736% -> 98.281%
func_8005D1CC: 99.159% -> 99.311%
func_8005CF60: 97.371% -> 98.510%, and fixes a real bug: the sprintf
call read `gRaceTrickAttackPointTotalForFormat`, a symbol that doesn't
exist anywhere else in the codebase or symbol_addrs.txt. Verified
against the raw target assembly that both the sprintf read and the
later threshold checks reference the same address as the real
`gRaceTrickAttackPointTotal` - the wrong name only ever compiled
because this function is still NON_MATCHING dead code; it would have
been an undefined reference at link time the moment it matched.

None reach 100% yet - all four remaining gaps are register-allocation
differences, not logic differences. Found via a mix of hand analysis
and an automated permuter pass; every result here is verified against
the isolated bootstrap workspace's own build.sh, not the permuter's
approximate internal score.
